caption: Study-level comparison of the 20 core full texts. Descriptions concern this review’s selected evaluation role, not an exhaustive inventory of each paper.
rows: Shen Y et al. [1]
Training: old model and labelled training data.
task metric compared with old/old baseline; backfill-free endpoint.
Criterion is task- and dataset-specific; geometry alone is not the criterion.
Hu W et al. [2]
Training: embedding training and historical transformations.
intended and unintended consumer task performance; multiple versions.
Compatibility includes downstream consumers; it is not solely nearest-neighbour matching.
Zhang B et al. [3]
Mixed refresh: compatible training and gallery backfill.
retrieval and negative flips during refresh; partial refresh.
Mixed-gallery competition needs evaluation beyond the old-only endpoint.
Zhang B et al. [4]
Training: old/new training data, prototypes.
face retrieval under five data/class split settings; backfill-free endpoint.
Training-overlap regimes are part of the compatibility claim.
Gao AK [5]
Paired translation: paired text embeddings.
held-out cosine; manual search examples; post-hoc endpoint.
High average cosine and manual examples do not establish representative labelled retrieval performance.
Jha R et al. [6]
Unpaired translation: disjoint unpaired embedding collections.
counterpart matching, cosine and information extraction; post-hoc endpoint.
The threat-model and matching evidence should be distinguished from production query-document relevance.
Dar G [7]
Unpaired translation: unpaired embedding sets.
counterpart Top-1, average rank and cosine; post-hoc endpoint.
Counterpart identity is an explicit evaluation target, rather than independently judged relevance.
Byun J et al. [8]
Adapter training: pre-extracted embeddings; no backbone update.
multimodal task retrieval and preservation; backfill-free endpoint.
No backbone update does not imply no adapter training or support-data requirement.
Bui N et al. [9]
Training: model training and uncertainty-aware alignment.
compatibility experiments; model generations.
Old representations need not be equally reliable targets for preservation.
Schnaus D et al. [10]
Unpaired translation: disjoint unimodal embeddings; optional pairs.
geometric correspondence and semantic transfer; post-hoc endpoint.
Coarse shared structure and exact sample-level recovery are different evidence targets.
Ramanujan V et al. [11]
Forward preparation: side-information stored at earlier deployment.
CMC and mAP compatibility retrieval; prepared future update.
The method requires preparation that cannot be reconstructed from arbitrary legacy vectors by assumption.
Meng Q et al. [12]
Training: training and cross-model compatibility constraints.
cross-model retrieval / recognition; cross-model endpoint.
Transformation direction and direct compatibility should be recorded separately.
Goyal A et al. [13]
System evaluation: synthetic histories; two small open-weight models.
answer accuracy and diagnostic decomposition; partial/full embedding migration.
Evidence is controlled and synthetic, not an operational deployment guarantee.
Rozmus M et al. [14]
Score mapping: synthetic query-document pairs.
score mapping and threshold portability; threshold migration.
A score conversion does not itself supply vector compatibility or relevance labels.
Gu B et al. [15]
Index migration: new embeddings and old graph.
ANNS quality and migration efficiency; index rebuilding.
Graph reuse reduces index reconstruction work; it does not eliminate document re-embedding.
Ricci S et al. [16]
Post-hoc alignment: alignment data and fitted transformation.
downstream compatibility and representation preservation; post-hoc endpoint.
Adaptation and preservation form a trade-off rather than an identical objective.
Ricci S et al. [17]
Post-hoc interpolation: paired support embeddings and old/new queries.
Recall@K; support-selected and oracle weights distinguished; backfill-free endpoint.
Local margin certification is already prior work; no novelty claim is made for our elementary bound.
Biondi N et al. [18]
Lifelong training: sequential learning with stationarity constraints.
multi-model empirical compatibility; multiple versions.
Testing one adjacent update does not establish all historical cross-version pairs.
Goswami D et al. [19]
Query compensation: continual training, distillation and drift estimation.
document retrieval over sequential tasks; fixed old corpus index.
Text retrieval compatibility is directly studied; this review must not claim the area is unstudied.
Jaeckle F et al. [20]
Partial backfill: alignment and original gallery for partial backfill.
retrieval improvement over backfill progress; partial refresh.
Migration trajectory and selected backfill order are explicit parts of evaluation.

caption: Five evidence targets and the extra evidence required for broader claims. These are synthesis categories rather than a new metric taxonomy.
rows: Coordinate approximation
Mapped and target vectors of the same evaluated item; specify normalization and error distribution.
Do query-specific errors remain small relative to candidate margins?
Same-item correspondence
A known counterpart is recovered from a specified distractor pool.
Are actual query-document relevance labels and distributions also tested?
Task relevance
Labelled retrieval or consumer-task outcomes under specified model directions.
Are the new homogeneous reference, subgroups and intermediate states covered?
Threshold behavior
Decision outcomes at a stated calibrated operating point.
Does recalibration preserve required error or utility on held-out labels?
Serving-index fidelity
Approximate versus exact retrieval over identical vectors and filters.
Are the underlying ranking and operational cutover separately acceptable?

caption: Closest prior contributions and the limited additional role of this synthesis. The comparison does not establish priority or completeness.
rows: BCT [1]; QDC [19]
Task-level new-to-old compatibility, including text retrieval in QDC.
Connect task tests to translation, calibration, index reuse and access constraints.
Hot-refresh [3]; FastFill [20]
Mixed-gallery regression and selective backfilling.
Retain trajectory as an independent obligation in a cross-family comparison.
vec2vec [6]; mini-vec2vec [7]
Unpaired translation, matching evidence and security implications.
Distinguish same-item matching from judged query-document relevance.
Score mapping [14]; graph migration [15]
Threshold portability and index-construction reuse.
Separate these interventions from avoiding document encoding.
Spherical interpolation [17]
Backward-compatible multimodal retrieval and local margin reasoning.
Use a conservative elementary bound only for exposition; claim no new margin theorem.
Operational runbooks [24-26]
Version isolation, re-embedding, validation and controlled cutover.
Link known operational practice to the research evidence targets and their non-implications.

caption: Proposed target-specific acceptance record. Numerical tolerances must be set for the application; no universal acceptance threshold is implied.
rows: Feasible intervention
Access to sources, weights, paired/unpaired support, side-information and old query encoders.
A method requiring unavailable resources appears deployable.
Vector / match quality
Direction; support/test split; dimensions; normalization; per-item errors; candidate pool.
Anchor success is interpreted as relevance or out-of-support performance.
Task compatibility
Old/old, new/new and deployed cross-version systems on paired held-out relevance queries.
Improvement over the old baseline is mistaken for full new-model recovery.
Trajectory stability
Refresh fraction and order, stable item population, query-level regressions.
Good homogeneous endpoints hide mixed-gallery failures.
Decision portability
Calibrated threshold or fusion rule, labels, acceptance/abstention outcomes.
Unchanged ordering is mistaken for unchanged decisions.
Search fidelity
Exact and approximate search on the same vectors, filters and search budgets.
Index approximation is confused with representation regression.
Practical acceptance
Encoding, fitting, storage, index-build and online costs; tested cutover and recovery.
Savings at one stage conceal cost or risk moved elsewhere.
